 Raiders-Seahawks: 17 Things we learned
 Seattle is too much for Las Vegas in Week 10
 by Bill Williamson Nov 16, 2026, 1:36 AM UTC Facebook 
 Link 
 Fernando Mendoza is going to be a good NFL Player.
 But there are going to lumps and predictably those lumps came Sunday in his starting debut.
 After scoring on their first two drives, Mendoza and the Raiders stalled as the stout Seattle Seahawks defense adjusted. The defending Super Bowl champions took over in the second half turning a 10-7 halftime deficit into a 21-13 victory, in a game that wasn’t as close as the score indicated. 
 Now, the Raiders are 4-6 and are in a big hole in the AFC as they have lost six of their past seven games after starting the season 3-0. The Raiders have not beaten a team with a winning record and they play at the Denver Broncos and the Cleveland Browns, both who have winning record, in the next two weeks. The Raiders are 1-4 at home.
 Here are some key aspects of the game:
 Mendoza’s day: 
 It started well as Mendoza scored on the Raiders’ first drive and then led them to a field goal on the second drive. Then the Raiders stalled. The Seahawks had the Raiders in a blender in the second half as went three and out on five straight drives. Mendoza ended up going 17 of 29 for 143 yards. He was poised and showed accuracy early. He was sacked six times and hit a lot. But he hung in there. Of course, the mature Mendoza said all the right things after the game and he put the failures on himself. He will be fine.
 Ugly streak over, but defense still lacking: 
 The Raiders’ defense ended their six-game streak of allowing, at least, 30 points. But it still wasn’t a good outing. Seattle backup quarterback Drew Lock made some big plays and Seattle ran for 150 yards. Seattle was sloppy on offense, but still dominated when it had to.
 Brutal second half: 
 The Raiders led 10-7 at the half and got the ball to start the second half. They were in good shape. Well, they should have been. The Seahawks dominated on both sides of the ball in the second half. The Raiders had 27 yards of offense in the second half and that included a 38-yard pass play from Mendoza to running back Ashton Jeanty. The Raiders didn’t get their first first down of the second half until there was less than four minutes left in the game.
 Missing Bowers: 
 Raiders’ star tight end Brock Bowers hurt his ankle early. He tried to play through it, but in the second quarter he left the game for good. Raiders coach Klint Kubiak had no update on Bowers’ injury after the game. it will clearly be a focal point of this week as the Raiders prepare to play Denver.
 Time of possession: 
 The Raiders went into the game with the fourth worst time-of-possession percentage in the league. They lost that battle again in Week 10, but it wasn’t awful. Seattle had the ball for 31:41 and the Raiders had it for 28:19.
 Season slipping away: 
 The Raiders’ 3-0 start seems like ages ago. They have lost six of their past seven games and are now two games under .500, erasing that great start to the Kubiak era.
 Run game brutal again: 
 Another week, another meager showing by the Raiders’ running game. Las Vegas had 65 yards rushing and Mendoza had 22 of those yards. Jeanty struggled again with just 18 yards on nine carries. Rookie Mike Washington had 23 yards Washington had 23 yards on eight carries. It’s just not there.
 Crosby has a big day: 
 Raiders’ star defensive end Maxx Crosby continued his hot play. He had four tackles for loss and has had, at least, one for five straight games. He’s had a sack in three straight games and has 5.5 on the season.
 No penalties: 
 The officials let them play Sunday. There weretwo penalties called all game, both on Seattle. No penalties and still Las Vegas wasn’t lose to winning this game.
 Two turnvoers: 
The Raiders had two turnovers for the second week in a row.
 Bad third quarter: 
 The Raiders had -minus two offensive yards on their first three series of the second half. They punted on all three drives.
 Seattle thin in trenches: 
 The Seahawks entered the game with left guard Quenton Nelson and left tackle Charles Cross on offense and star defensive tackle Leonard Williams on defense. During the game, they lost right tackle Abe Lucas and defensive tackle Jarran Reed.
 What a start: 
 The Raiders forced Drew Lock into a lost fumble on the second play of the game. Mendoza took his first snap as a starter in Seattle territory and the Mendoza ran it for a 10-yard touchdown run on third and goal to take a 7-0 lead. Las Vegas couldn’t have asked for a better start.
 Stokes hurt: 
 Cornerback Eric Stokes appeared to hurt his hand in the third quarter, He was replaced by rookie Jermod McCoy. Stokes returned in the third quarter.
 Masses starts: 
The revolving door at an outside cornerback spot continued as fifth-round pick Zeke Masses started over Darien Porter and Jermod McCoy. It was Masses’ first start since Week 5 and his fifth start of the season. Masses struggled in the third quarter and was replaced by previous starter, Darien Porter.
 Four tight ends: 
 The Raiders elevated tight end Carter Runyon from the practice squad for the game and he joined Brock Bowers, Michael Mayer and Ian Thomas on the game-day roster.
 Fan takeover: 
This is nothing new, but their were many, many Seahawks fans at Allegiant Stadium on Sunday. Seattle fans travel week and they showed up in Las Vegas. This was the Seahawks’ first regular-season game in Las Vegas.
